entries.title: Fixed Offset Shafts and Orthogonal Key Disc Coupling
entries.description: One independently authored complete static offset-parallel-shaft connector display. A single broad foot supports two whole pedestals and complete bored bearing sleeves at different fixed heights. Two horizontal collared shafts terminate in two entire circular hubs, one with a real vertical recessed inward groove and the other with a perpendicular horizontal groove. One central closed disc has two integral full raised tongues on its opposite faces; the complete keys enter the matching real slots, while broad exposed axial sections of each fixed tongue make their perpendicular relation readable. Display spacing is intentionally extended for visibility, not an engineering proportion or operating configuration. All disc faces, finite slot floors/sidewalls, raised-key risers and peripheral walls are newly authored continuous material surfaces; not separate blocks pasted on old disks. No old Cardan forks/trunnions, drawing-trammel plates/sliders or other asset geometry imported. This is one whole Oldham-style illustrative connection assembly, zero scenes and no extra counted components. Four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres, Z up and horizontal-bounds-centred whole ground sole. Fixed artistic overlaps and intervals only; no working fit, sliding, velocity, torque/power transmission, shaft compatibility, lubrication, manufacture, load, installation, engineering or safety claims. Rigging, motion and interaction are not produced or verified.

entries.title: Fixed Open Races and Pocketed Ball Bearing
entries.description: One newly authored whole static open ball-bearing appearance. Two complete concentric thick annular races have genuinely concave opposed grooves around a row of complete rounded balls. The central shaft bore is entirely open. One complete continuous lower annular cage with full upright separators defines actual upper-open ball pockets; this is an open comb-like cage, not claimed closed ball windows or a sealed bearing. Its low ring intentionally engages the fixed ball bottoms. Race and ball clearances are fixed illustrative separations, not running fits. No old gimbal, single bored rod-end sphere, shaft, pedestal or machine mesh imported. Three opaque constant PBR materials, metres, Z up and full horizontal-bounds-centred ground origin; one prop, zero scenes. Static display only: no rolling, friction, speed, precision, lubrication, bearing fit, load or torque transfer, installation, manufacture or mechanical safety claim.
